concepts.label: A
concepts.name: Peakback Trout
concepts.brief: Title 'A · PEAKBACK TROUT'. A strong right-facing blue trout silhouette, with its dorsal outline becoming one angular mountain peak. A broad paper-colored winding river cut crosses the lower body and opens at the edge; gold eye. Restrained evergreen belly accent. Mountain and river are structural parts of the fish, not a landscape framed inside it. Full angular tail, balanced compact proportions, one peak only; no pine forest, scenery, frame or fish scale details.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create ONE new logo concept for OREGON FISH FORECAST, an approachable Oregon river-conditions website. The reference image shows the earlier logo family: use its blue/gold/evergreen identity as grounding, not as a design to copy. This round should be more compact and graphic to fit an illustrated outdoor field-guide homepage.

Create a square 2048x2048 brand proof on warm paper #F5F2E9. Same layout: small concept title at top left; one large colored symbol centered above the exact two-line wordmark 'OREGON' / 'FISH FORECAST'; generous whitespace; a thin rule near the bottom; below it a smaller single-blue-ink version at left labeled 'ONE COLOR' and a small reversed-white version on a blue square at right labeled 'SMALL SIZE'. Repeat the SAME mark faithfully in all three treatments. No extra symbols or concepts. Wordmark in clean bold DM Sans-style capitals, OREGON larger with subtle tracking.

Flat vector-style geometry and crisp edges, recognizable silhouette, deliberate negative space. Blue #002A86, evergreen #285D45, restrained gold #FFEA0F; paper as negative space. No gradients, texture, shadows, mockup objects, clipart, photorealism or intricate scenic detail. Single-color mark must work without relying on color boundaries. This is a raster concept proof, not a website screen.

concepts.label: B
concepts.name: Timbercut Trout
concepts.brief: Title 'B · TIMBERCUT TROUT'. A compact right-facing trout built from bold, slightly squared woodcut-inspired shapes with confident chamfered edges. ONE large paper-colored pine cutout creates the gill region, using three broad branch tiers. Short evergreen belly shape, restrained gold eye. Looks like a beautifully designed field-guide stamp without distressed texture or an enclosing badge. No mountain panorama, forest of tiny trees, thin outlines or decorative scales.

concepts.label: C
concepts.name: Confluence Trout
concepts.brief: Title 'C · CONFLUENCE TROUT'. A streamlined right-facing trout assembled from two substantial blue and evergreen shapes, divided by one wide Y-shaped paper river channel. The two tributaries merge into a broad river opening along the lower silhouette. Gold eye anchors the head. Clearly recognizable tail and dorsal fin. Elegant, flowing, symmetrical visual weight; only essential contours. The Y channel stays open and legible in the one-color proof. No separate mountain, forest, frame or background landscape.

The fish itself forms the circular silhouette; do not place a fish inside a ring. Blue body, one broad evergreen current segment, tiny gold eye. Minimal fin shapes convey a fish without aggression. No interior landscape or surrounding badge. Distinctive compact app-icon potential; confident flat flowing shape.

concepts.label: E
concepts.name: Headwaters Pennant
concepts.brief: Title 'E · HEADWATERS PENNANT'. A compact vertical trail-sign pennant with a broad upper edge and tapered lower point. One mountain cut defines its crown; one wide winding paper river flows down through a green lower field and opens at the lower point. Blue outer mass, restrained small gold sun accent. Three substantial shapes maximum, bold legible negative space. The OREGON FISH FORECAST wordmark supplies the fishing identity; no fish silhouette required. No circular badge, tiny forest, decorative border or distant scenic illustration.

concepts.label: F
concepts.name: River Gate
concepts.brief: Title 'F · RIVER GATE'. An open mountain-shaped blue arch above two broad flowing water strokes. One evergreen water stroke ends in a subtle but legible fish-tail notch. A restrained gold sun disc sits off-center near the peak. Architectural, open, grounded, balanced. Generous gaps between the arch and currents; the mark should read as mountains and flowing water immediately. No surrounding enclosure, full fish silhouette or tiny fish hidden in the negative space. Few expressive shapes; avoid a generic roof or wireless-signal icon.
